# Put it into Practice {.unnumbered}

Now it's time to try things out for yourself. Complete each of the following steps, based on what we learned in this chapter.

::: {.content-visible unless-profile="excel"}
Unless your instructor tells you otherwise, use an [do-file]{.content-visible when-profile="stata"}[R script]{.content-visible when-profile="r"} to execute all code needed to accomplish the following (note: step 1 can be completed outside of [Stata]{.content-visible when-profile="stata"}[R]{.content-visible when-profile="r"}):
:::

1.  Load in the World Development Indicators dataset (`development.dta`).[^03-lab-1] You can download it [here](https://learndata.net/development.dta) and save it on your computer. [Or you can load the file directly into Stata through the Internet with the following URL: <https://learndata.net/development.dta>]{.content-visible when-profile="stata"} [Or you can load the file directly into R through the Internet with the following URL: <https://learndata.net/development.dta>]{.content-visible when-profile="r"}

2.  Select three variables to examine. Choose variables that have **not** already been transformed (transformed variables have names starting with `log_` or `z_` or ending with `_z` or `_01`).

3.  For each of your three variables, create at least one transformation of the variable.

4.  Generate a table of summary statistics that includes both the untransformed and transformed versions of your three variables.

5.  For each possible pairing of your three untransformed variables, find the correlation coefficient and create a scatter plot. Note that there should be three pairings in all (if your variables are A, B, and C, the pairings are: (1) A with B, (2) A with C, and (3) B with C).

6.  Run a few different regressions (at least three) using different combinations of the transformed and untransformed versions of your three variables (you can mix and match).

[^03-lab-1]: This is a modified version of data obtained from The World Bank: <https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037712/world-development-indicators> ([CC-BY 4.0](https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/public-licenses?fragment=cc))

::: {.content-visible unless-profile="excel"}
After completing all of this, you should save your [do-file]{.content-visible when-profile="stata"}[R script]{.content-visible when-profile="r"} in a folder that is convenient to access. If you are submitting work to an instructor, they will likely want you to send them both your [do-file]{.content-visible when-profile="stata"}[R script]{.content-visible when-profile="r"} and a Word doc containing your results for items 4-6.
:::
